title: XR_SAMPLE_controller_pulse
ask: tighten my draft of this extension section, OpenXR spec style.
rules: Plain verbs, no puffery, no stock AI words.

samples.title: 12.31.1 Overview · XR_SAMPLE_eye_blink
samples.text: This extension reports when the user blinks. The runtime sends one event per blink. Applications can use it to hide scene changes. It does not report gaze direction.

samples.title: 12.36.3 Description · xrGetHandPoseSAMPLE
samples.text: xrGetHandPoseSAMPLE returns the latest pose of one hand. The runtime MUST fill poseInfo->joints in the order given by XrHandJointSAMPLE. If tracking is lost, the runtime MUST set isActive to XR_FALSE. Applications should check isActive before reading joints.

style_notes: Opens with the subject: "This extension", "The runtime", or the function name.
One fact per sentence. Few "because" or "so that" chains.
Present tense, plain verbs: "reports", "returns", not "allows" or "is able to".

options.text: This extension allows applications to send a short haptic pulse to a controller that is being tracked by the runtime.
This extension lets an application send a short haptic pulse to a tracked controller.
This extension adds a way to trigger a single, short haptic pulse on a tracked controller.
This extension sends a short haptic pulse to a tracked controller.
Because the pulse has a fixed shape and a fixed length, a runtime is able to play it with lower latency than a general vibration.
The pulse has a fixed shape and length, so runtimes can play it with lower latency than a general vibration.
A fixed shape and length let the runtime play the pulse with lower latency.
The pulse has a fixed shape and length. The runtime can play it with low latency.
Applications which need to control amplitude, frequency or duration should use xrApplyHapticFeedback instead.
Applications that need to control amplitude, frequency or duration should use xrApplyHapticFeedback.
For control over amplitude, frequency or duration, use xrApplyHapticFeedback.
Applications that need amplitude, frequency or duration control should use xrApplyHapticFeedback.

parts.label: New functions

options.text: xrSendControllerPulseSAMPLE plays one pulse on the controller identified by pulseInfo->subactionPath.
xrSendControllerPulseSAMPLE plays one pulse on the controller given by pulseInfo->subactionPath.
Calling xrSendControllerPulseSAMPLE plays a pulse on the controller at pulseInfo->subactionPath.
If a pulse is already playing on that controller, the runtime MUST replace it with the new pulse.
If a pulse is already playing there, the runtime MUST replace it.
A new pulse replaces one that is still playing.

parts.label: Valid usage (implicit)
parts.text:
- The XR_SAMPLE_controller_pulse extension MUST be enabled prior to calling xrSendControllerPulseSAMPLE
- session MUST be a valid XrSession handle
- pulseInfo MUST be a pointer to a valid XrControllerPulseInfoSAMPLE structure

options.text: Note: Runtimes on devices without a haptic motor should return XR_SUCCESS and do nothing, so that applications do not need a separate code path.
Note: On devices with no haptic motor, runtimes should return XR_SUCCESS and play nothing, so applications need no separate code path.
Note: If the device has no haptic motor, the runtime should still return XR_SUCCESS so applications keep one code path.
